title: Finite-free scalar transport of the normalized Roos comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes $W$ below are noetherian and finite dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, with the meaning and the common full integral constructible categories of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $R_{E,W}=\lim_{n\geq1}(A_{E,n})_W$ on the small pro-etale site, and use framework and PBC completed pullbacks $F^s_{h,E},F^p_{h,E}$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Write $I_{W,E}$ for restriction along the quotient-normalized coefficient identity, giving the integral identity equivalence. All equalities below use these fixed identity transports; we suppress $I$ when source and target already have the same module presentation. For a scheme isomorphism $h:U\simeq T$, let $G_{h,E}$ be ordinary derived module pullback on the completed rings. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ over $R_{E,T}$ set
$$Q_{h,E}(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T),\qquad H(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Q)[-1],$$
with the actual quotient transitions and $s_Q((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].
For each such tower, use the normalized derived comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison],
$$\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q,$$
where $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms and $\iota_I:\lim I_\bullet\to H(I_\bullet)$ has coordinates $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Write $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}:IF^s_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,E}I$ for this comparison with the defining realization identifications, and $b^{\rm int}_{h,E}$ for its restriction to the full integral constructible categories.
For $E\subset L$, put $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ and use $\chi_W:C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_W$, $d_\bullet$, $\delta^s$, $\delta^p=\alpha^p$ and $\alpha^s=F^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\delta^s\chi_U^{-1}$ with the actual normalization specified in [lem-fd-scalar-pullback-realization-identification]. The finite-free tensor product/limit transport carries $C_U(\rho_Q)$ to $\rho_{C_UQ}$, under the canonical product and limit identifications, with the universal units retained. In particular for every integral constructible $K$ one has, in the actual realized whole-diagram models,
$$b_{h,L,C_TK}\circ\delta^s_K=\delta^p_{IK}\circ C_U(b_{h,E,K}).$$
This equality retains the strict quotient transitions and derived-limit counit. The completion-conjugated equality is
$$F^p_{h,L}(\chi_T^{-1})\circ b_{h,L,S_TK}\circ\alpha^s_K
=\alpha^p_{IK}\circ C_U(b_{h,E,K})\circ\chi_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}^{-1}.$$
Here $b=b^{\rm int}$ with the coefficient identity transports inserted. Write $J_{W,E}$ for the raw rationalization of $I_{W,E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-pbc-rational-category], $P_W$ for rational PBC scalar extension, $b_{h,E}$ also for the raw rationalization, and $j_W=\chi_W^{-1}[1/\varpi_L]$. Then
$$F^p_{h,L}(j_T)\circ b_{h,L,S_TK}\circ J_{U,L}(\alpha^s_K)
=\alpha^p_{J_{T,E}K}\circ P_U(b_{h,E,K})\circ j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}.$$
The inverse of the localized integral $b$ is the rational finite-datum component. These statements use raw localization on integral objects and tensor morphisms, with no Karoubi completion.

proof.text: On $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ write $R=R_{E,U}$, $S=R_{L,U}$ and $C=C_U$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is finite free over $R$. Termwise tensor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-strict-tower-transport]. It preserves countable products: after choosing an $R$-basis of $S$ its underlying $R$-module functor is a finite direct sum of identities, and the canonical comparison rearranges the two indices of $(M_{n,j})_{n,j}$; its projections are tensor of the source projections. This comparison is $S$-linear, so the underlying inverse is $S$-linear too. Countable products are exact in both module categories by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus the exact product-preserving functor theorem applies to $C$, on the small site in the chosen module universe.

proof.text:
Let $\kappa_X:CH(X)\to H(CX)$ be the canonical product map on both cone coordinates and $\lambda_X:CR\lim X\to R\lim(CX)$ the finite-free limit comparison. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Its signed coordinates $(x,z)$ correspond to our coordinates $(y,x)$ by $z=-y$: the differential becomes $(dx,(1-s)x-dz)$ and the inclusion remains $(x,0)$. Both product maps are diagonal, so this sign change conjugates its $\theta$ to $\rho^{-1}$ with exactly the normalization of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Its conjugation formula is therefore
$$\lambda_X C(\rho_X)=\rho_{CX}\kappa_X.$$
The theorem also says this is the ordinary limit/tensor map followed by a resolution of the image tower. Hence it is the actual comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-strict-tower-transport], rather than an unspecified triangle isomorphism. Explicitly, choose $q:X\to I$ and $r:CI\to J$ with injective-term K-injective targets, and write $\beta:C\lim I\to\lim CI$ for the ordinary comparison. If $e_I:\Delta\lim I\to I$ and $e_J:\Delta\lim J\to J$ are the strict limit cones, then
$$r\,C(e_I)=e_J\,\Delta((\lim r)\beta).$$
Indeed its $n$th tower component on either side is $r_nC(\mathrm{pr}_n)$; this is equality of strict tower chain maps. Localizing and inserting $q^{-1},r^{-1}$ gives the counit equation for the specified $\lambda$. No claim that $CI$ is K-injective is needed.

proof.text:
Take $X=Q_{h,E}(P)$ and $Y=Q_{h,L}(P\otimes R_{L,T})$. By [lem-fd-pullback-common-strict-tower-models], $b_E,b_L$ are the normalized $\rho_X,\rho_Y$ in the actual defining realizations and are natural isomorphisms on the full integral categories. By [lem-fd-scalar-pullback-realization-identification], the actual whole tower map $d:CX\to Y$ gives $\delta^s=H(d)\kappa_X$ and $\delta^p=R\lim(d)\lambda_X=\alpha^p$. Naturality of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] and Step 2 give
$$\rho_Y H(d)\kappa_X=R\lim(d)\rho_{CX}\kappa_X=R\lim(d)\lambda_X C(\rho_X).$$
Insert the defining realization identifications: this is $b_{h,L,C_TK}\delta^s_K=\delta^p_{IK}C_U(b_{h,E,K})$. All arrows come from strict tower maps and the normalized derived-limit comparison; thus the quotient transitions and counit of Step 2 are retained. Resolution independence and restriction to integral constructible objects follow from the two cited realization statements.

proof.text:
The formula in [lem-fd-scalar-pullback-realization-identification] is $\alpha^s=F^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\delta^s\chi_U^{-1}$, with $\delta^p=\alpha^p$. Naturality of the isomorphism $b_L$ from [lem-fd-pullback-common-strict-tower-models] at $\chi_T$ gives
$$F^p_{h,L}(\chi_T^{-1})b_{h,L,S_TK}F^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)=b_{h,L,C_TK}.$$
Substitution followed by Step 3 gives the required integral equation
$$F^p_{h,L}(\chi_T^{-1})b_{h,L,S_TK}\alpha^s_K=\alpha^p_{IK}C_U(b_{h,E,K})\chi_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}^{-1}.$$
The fixed coefficient identity transports are inserted at each source and target. These are cancellations of natural isomorphisms between the stated functors.

proof.text:
Apply raw localization to Step 4. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-pbc-rational-category] it keeps integral objects and sends $f$ to $f\otimes1$. It preserves composition and inverses, so $\chi^{-1}$ becomes $j$. By [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] ordinary integral $C_U$ and its actual pullback comparison rationalize to $P_U$ and $\alpha^p$. Thus the localized equation is
$$F^p_{h,L}(j_T)b_{h,L,S_TK}J_{U,L}(\alpha^s_K)=\alpha^p_{J_{T,E}K}P_U(b_{h,E,K})j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}.$$
Finally [lem-fd-pullback-augmentation-counit-matching] states that $(b^{\rm int})^{-1}$, its ambient lift and raw rationalization supply the normalized finite datum. Since localization preserves inverse, the component is precisely the inverse of this same localized $b$. No idempotents or objects are added.
